A1.reason: It shows rows added and updated per table, the columns touched, how many rows hold the fixed status value, and whether anything outside the agreement was touched. That covers C2 and C4, and part of C1.

A2.reason: The A1 rehearsal runs before the promotion and the tidy. A rehearsal at A2 is taken after the promotion and the tidy, so it can show that the undo still works once the working copies are cleared (C7).

C1.for_what_part: These answers read the staged set against the approved list. They do not read the live tables, so only the promotion's line in the record ties the live tables to that set.

C2.for_what_part: They show 100 case rows added, 100 account rows updated and how many hold the fixed value, all on the staged set. They do not show one case per customer, and they do not show the live tables.

C4.for_what_part: It shows no other table or column touched and no deletions in the staged set. It does not show the live tables after the promotion.

C6.for_what_part: It shows the undo on a copy of the live tables. It holds only if the promotion starts from the state the rehearsal ran on, and only for one hour.

C7.for_what_part: It shows the undo works on a copy taken after the tidy. It speaks only for the time it was taken.

C8.for_what_part: It shows the recipients match those promoted, the wording matches the approved wording, and the number to send. It does not show the notices were ordered, which is the later sending.

C9.for_what_part: It shows the confirmed and the unconfirmed sending calls, and their recipients and wording against the release. It speaks only as of the time it was taken, and a call ordered but not confirmed stays in doubt.

parsed.what_i_would_have_wanted_and_the_library: C3 needs the requester's rule applied to each account, and no instrument does that. C5 needs scope of a call on the read lines, and that can only be asked for during the work, once the lines exist. C10 needs trace of a call on the sending lines at A3, also only available once the lines exist. No instrument reads the live tables after the promotion, so C1, C2 and C4 rest on the staged set plus the promotion's line in the record. I kept the plan at 180 of the 200 allowed. A second undo rehearsal at A3 or a same set at A2 would have gone over budget and would mostly repeat answers already in the plan.
